channel.name: S1
channel.notes: 10.65 GHz channel group; its footprints span the same scan as the other groups.

applicability.basis: JAXA moved GCOM-W1 to regular observation on 2012-08-10 and lists GCOM-W (AMSR2 mounted) in operation at retrieval on 2026-10-27. The end is the evidence cutoff, not a mission end date.

evidence.title: Conical Scanner Validation: AMSR2
evidence.document_revision: TAT-C 3.6.0 validation notebook; 2026-09-26 L1C data and 2026-10-04 TLE
evidence.excerpt: AMSR2's lines of sight lie on a cone 47.56 deg from nadir to within about 0.1 deg across the whole scan (an incidence angle of about 55 deg at the ground). The observed arc spans scan azimuths from -74.8 to +75.8 deg (a sector of about 75.3 deg on either side, sampled every 0.62 deg), centered within about 0.5 deg of the inertial velocity at all latitudes, but up to 4.3 deg from the Earth-fixed velocity.
evidence.interpretation: Cone angle, product-sector center and half width, inertial velocity frame, sample spacing, and the separation of cone angle from ground incidence.

evidence.title: Conical Scanner Validation: AMSR2
evidence.document_revision: TAT-C 3.6.0 validation notebook; 2026-09-26 L1C data and 2026-10-04 TLE
evidence.excerpt: the line of sight to each footprint (on the ellipsoid) is computed from the spacecraft position at the scan time and decomposed into a cone angle (from the geodetic nadir) and a scan azimuth
evidence.interpretation: The measured cone angle uses the geodetic nadir.

evidence.title: Conical Scanner Validation: AMSR2
evidence.document_revision: TAT-C 3.6.0 validation notebook; 2026-09-26 L1C data and 2026-10-04 TLE
evidence.excerpt: a ConicalInstrument with the measured cone angle and scan sector (center and half width), in the inertial velocity frame, and a 1 deg along-track field of view (its footprint is the region the arc sweeps as the satellite moves along track by the distance this angle subtends at nadir, about 12 km).
evidence.interpretation: The 1 degree along-track field of view is an explicit approximation for integration-time motion and footprint width.

evidence.title: GCOM-W (AMSR2 mounted): AMSR2 Specifications
evidence.locator: AMSR2 Specifications and Channel Set, 10.65 GHz row
evidence.excerpt: Swath width: Nominal 1450 km, effective 1620 km. The performance guarantee range is +/-61 degrees scanning angle (1450km). The product contains data for a scanning angle of +/-75 degrees (1620km). Incidence angle: Nominal 55 degrees. 10.65 GHz: beam width 1.2 degrees.
evidence.interpretation: JAXA separates the nominal performance guarantee sector from the wider product sector, and the nominal ground incidence angle from a cone angle. The 10.65 GHz beam width describes the channel.

evidence.title: GCOM-W (AMSR2 mounted)
evidence.excerpt: GCOM-W (AMSR2 mounted) [In Operation]. International Designation Code 2012-025A. Launch Date May 18, 2012. Sun-Synchronous Subrecurrent/Recurrent. Altitude 700km. Inclination Approx. 98 degrees.
evidence.interpretation: Confirms spacecraft identity and in-operation status at retrieval.

evidence.title: SHIZUKU (GCOM-W1) Regular Observation Operations
evidence.excerpt: JAXA completed the initial functional verification of the Global Change Observation Mission 1st - Water "SHIZUKU" (GCOM-W1) and has moved to the regular observation operation on August 10 as scheduled.
evidence.interpretation: Establishes the applicability start; earlier commissioning data is not claimed.

source_revision.authority: TAT-C 3.6.0 validation and JAXA GCOM-W/AMSR2 specifications
source_revision.summary: TAT-C supplies the measured cone and sector in the inertial frame; JAXA supplies the nominal/product sector distinction, ground incidence meaning, channel beam width, and mission status.

interpretation.summary: AMSR2 on GCOM-W1 is a forward-looking conical scanner in the inertial velocity frame using the wider product sector measured by TAT-C. The cone angle is from geodetic nadir, not the roughly 55 degree ground incidence angle.
limitations: Cone and sector values are one-day medians; per-scan and per-channel variation is not modeled.
The 1 degree along-track field of view approximates integration-time motion and footprint width, not a measured integration time.
The product sector is wider than JAXA's nominal performance guarantee; results describe the product scan.
Applicability ends at the source retrieval date, not a documented mission end date.
The TAT-C mission comparison covers one analysis day and is not a general mission-accuracy claim.

approximations.description: A fixed 1 degree along-track field of view stands in for integration-time arc motion and footprint width.
approximations.impact: The cone-crossing epoch is not moved, but footprint extent and the in-view validity check depend on this approximation.

approximations.description: Cone angle, scan center, and half width are medians from one day of L1C footprint centers; scan jitter and channel variation are not modeled.
approximations.impact: The TAT-C validation matched 99.95% of passes with a 0.27 s p95 epoch residual; this is not a mission-accuracy guarantee.

source_conflicts.description: JAXA gives a nominal performance-guarantee sector of +/-61 degrees (1450 km) and a wider product sector of +/-75 degrees (1620 km); TAT-C measured 75.332 degrees from product footprints.

options.summary: Product sector: +/-75 degrees, 1620 km; measured 75.332 degrees.

source_conflicts.rationale: The study uses the product sector because the TAT-C validation measured 75.332 degrees and matched 99.95% of observed passes. The nominal sector is a different configuration and its width is not combined with the measured product angles.

source_conflicts.description: JAXA's nominal 55 degree incidence angle is at the ground; TAT-C requires the 47.564 degree angle from nadir.

options.summary: Nominal ground incidence 55 degrees; not a cone angle.
Measured cone angle 47.564 degrees from geodetic nadir.

source_conflicts.rationale: TAT-C consumes the angle from nadir; the 55 degree ground incidence value remains context only.

source_conflicts.description: The arc center is within about 0.5 degrees of inertial velocity but up to 4.3 degrees from Earth-fixed velocity.

options.summary: Earth-fixed velocity frame aligned with the ground track.
Inertial velocity frame aligned with the orbit plane.

source_conflicts.rationale: The validation measured the arc center within about 0.5 degree of inertial velocity, so the study uses the inertial frame.
